name: butter pie crust
instructions:
The house pie crust, two variants. NOTE: THIS IS NOT THE GALETTE CRUST — the ATK whole wheat galette crust with white vinegar is a separate (still untranscribed) recipe.

THE FAT RULE (both variants): you need 1/2 CUP OF FAT, and you can MIX/MATCH BUTTER AND SHORTENING freely within it.

=== VARIANT A — BUTTER PIE CRUST (PLAIN) ===

- 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup fat (butter and/or shortening — see fat notes)

Bake at 400°F.

=== VARIANT B — WHOLE WHEAT (SAVORY) ===

- 1 cup all-purpose flour + 1/2 cup wheat flour
- 1 tbsp sugar
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1/2 cup fat (butter and/or shortening)

Bake at 400°F. The wheat flour tilts it savory — this is the variant for the savory pies.
notes:
NOT THE GALETTE CRUST: the ATK whole wheat galette crust (with white vinegar) is a different dough — perfect for galettes, recipe still to be transcribed (see [[sweet-potato-pies-and-galettes]]). This recipe is the standard pie crust.

=== FAT — 1/2 CUP, MIX AND MATCH ===

You need 1/2 cup of fat; butter and shortening can be mixed and matched in any ratio. Character guide: SHORTENING makes the crust easier to form and stretchier; BUTTER makes it flaky/brittle.

LARD INSTEAD OF SHORTENING: lard subs 1:1 for the shortening share and gives noticeably better flavor — savory, slightly meaty depth. Use lard when the filling can stand a less-neutral crust (most savory fillings, anything mushroom or meat); stick with shortening when the filling wants fully neutral.

=== RATIO NOTE ===

Some recipes call for a much higher flour-to-fat ratio, but this works well enough for a brittle/flaky crust.

=== PAN SIZE ===

This recipe fits an 11-inch pie tray exactly. Scale up or down for other sizes.

=== USERS ===

[[chicken-pot-pie]] (real pie top), [[french-quiche]], [[tomato-tart]], [[sweet-potato-pies-and-galettes]] (stand-in until the ATK galette crust is transcribed).
